notices.start: Kansas law contains important requirements you must follow
notices.end: affect your ability to file a lawsuit.
notices.quote_note: none: the wording is not in quotation marks; it follows 'Such notice shall be in substantially the following form:' and the state file says it 'begins at "Kansas law contains" and ends at "file a lawsuit."'

changes.support: The first pass proposed a home-made "pre-suit notice acknowledgment"; the statutory text should be used instead.

unsure: KS-60-4706: stored on file, not printed, because the act defines 'contractor' as one 'engaged in the business of constructing dwellings' and 'dwelling' narrowly (not manufactured homes), and the state file says it is not settled whether a remodel-only trade is covered; the builder only knows residential or not.
KS-cancel: the invited-visit repair exclusion (50-640(c)(1)(E)) depends on facts the builder does not know, so the notice is held in any case.
KS: K.S.A. 60-4707 (list of subcontractors to the buyer of a new dwelling, within 30 days after the sale closes) is handed over after the sale and only for new dwellings, so no notice was added.

KS-cancel and KS-cancel-form: printed for any job sold at the customer's home; the statute's exclusions (consumer asked the supplier to visit to repair or maintain property, emergency waiver, consumer-credit rescission) turn on facts the builder does not know.
